beny-steinmetz.total: In a sworn statement to the ICSID tribunal in the Simandou case he described BSG Resources, into which the group's natural-resource projects were consolidated in 2003 and which he advises, as having operations in 14 countries, having employed over 8,000 people, and having evaluated more than 120 prospective deals on four continents over the previous decade (Witness Statement of Benjamin Steinmetz, BSG Resources Ltd v Republic of Guinea, ICSID Case No. ARB/14/22, 2 September 2015).

sources_add.title: Witness Statement of Benjamin Steinmetz, 2 September 2015 (BSG Resources Limited v Republic of Guinea, ICSID Case No. ARB/14/22)
sources_add.publisher: International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes

beny-steinmetz.note: Opened his own witness statement filed in the ICSID arbitration, hosted on the ICSID (World Bank) site. The figures are his own, given in paragraphs 12 and 14; he attaches no year to the 14-country and 8,000-employee figures, so the sentence credits them to the statement rather than dating them. The same statement says the wider BSG group 'now operates in more than 20 countries worldwide' and that he holds no board seat, directorship or shareholding in BSGR, acting under an advisory contract. BSGR publishes no annual report, so no independently audited group figure was found.

bill-turner.total: As Anvil Mining's president and chief executive from 8 January 2004, he ran a company with three producing mines, Dikulushi, Kulu and Kinsevere, all in the Democratic Republic of Congo, exploration interests in the DRC, Zambia and the Philippines, and 4,390 people at its operations as of 29 February 2008, 2,750 of them direct employees (Anvil Mining Limited, Annual Information Form for the year ended 31 December 2007).

sources_add.title: Anvil Mining Limited, Annual Information Form for the financial year ended 31 December 2007 (dated 28 March 2008)
sources_add.publisher: Anvil Mining Limited, filed with the Australian Securities Exchange

bill-turner.note: Opened Anvil's Annual Information Form on the ASX announcements server (two passes, characters 0-100,000 and 100,000-200,000). The document states his appointment date (president and CEO and director since 8 January 2004; managing director of Anvil Mining NL July 2003 to January 2004; general manager July 1995 to July 2003), so the company-scale figures fall inside his tenure. Employee breakdown in the document: Dikulushi 1,360, Kulu 760, Kinsevere 1,730, other locations 540. The document gives no total count of exploration licences, so none is claimed. The Kilwa killings were in October 2004; this report is the earliest filing of his tenure I could open that states a company-wide headcount, so the headcount is 2008, not 2004.

ira-rennert.total: He is chairman and chief executive of The Renco Group, which through trusts he established controls The Doe Run Resources Corporation; in the year to 31 October 2001 Doe Run ran eight production shafts along Missouri's Viburnum Trend plus the La Oroya smelter and the Cobriza mine in Peru, employed 400 salaried and 1,138 hourly staff in the United States and 955 salaried, 2,131 hourly and 1,475 contract workers in Peru, and had net sales of $303.1 million in the United States and $434.3 million in Peru (Doe Run Resources Corporation, Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 31 October 2001, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission).

sources_add.title: The Doe Run Resources Corporation, Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 31 October 2001

ira-rennert.note: Downloaded and read the full 10-K text from SEC EDGAR. The filing states Renco Group is owned by trusts Rennert established, that he is Renco's chairman and chief executive, and that he therefore controls Doe Run and its subsidiaries. The figures are Doe Run's, not Renco Group's: renco-group.com blocks automated reading (robots_disallowed), and the Renco Metals 10-K for fiscal 1999 that search returned gives figures only for Magcorp (503 employees) and Sabel (241), not for the group. So no group-wide Renco figure is given. Blocked URLs: https://www.renco-group.com/

iskandar-safa.total: As Privinvest's chairman, a full-time executive post in which, the English High Court found, 'no major activity proceeded without his knowledge and approval', he signed three supply contracts in 2013 and 2014 with Mozambican state companies for maritime surveillance, a tuna fleet and a shipyard, worth, after change orders, approaching US$2 billion, or more than 12 per cent of Mozambique's GDP (High Court of Justice, Business and Property Courts, Republic of Mozambique v Credit Suisse International and others, judgment of 29 July 2024).

sources_add.publisher: High Court of Justice of England and Wales, Business and Property Courts (Commercial Court)

iskandar-safa.note: Opened the judgment PDF (first 100,000 characters) and read the passages on Privinvest's description (para 20), Safa's role (paras 26, 29, 30) and the contracts (paras 6, 7, 89, 90, 118). No group-wide count of shipyards, employees or countries was found in any source I could open: the shipyards.gr directory entry lists three associated yards and no totals; an undated interview with Safa in The CEO Magazine claims Privinvest has delivered 2,000 vessels, but it carries no date and no yard, employee or revenue count, so I left it out of the sentence. joseph-stiglitz.figure_for_owner: World Bank fiscal 1998 and fiscal 1999 (1 July 1997 to 30 June 1999): the Bank's executive directors approved 229 IBRD/IDA lending operations in fiscal 1998 (105 IBRD loans, 124 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1998, Appendix 14) and 276 in fiscal 1999 (131 IBRD loans, 145 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1999, Appendix 14) - 505 over the two years, which is this map's sum of the two reports. What that counts: IBRD loans and IDA credits approved by the Board. Both appendices state that supplements are included in the amounts but are not counted as separate lending operations, and that joint IBRD/IDA operations are counted once, as IBRD operations. It excludes IFC and MIGA entirely, and excludes GEF, Montreal Protocol, guarantees, recipient-executed trust-fund activities, carbon offset, special financing and debt-reduction operations. Why these two years: the officer lists in the annual reports, dated 30 June 1997, 30 June 1998 and 30 June 1999, each name 'Joseph E. Stiglitz, Senior Vice President, Development Economics, and Chief Economist', and his Nobel autobiography says 'I left the World Bank in January 2000', so fiscal 1998 and 1999 are the two full fiscal years wholly inside the period he is recorded in the post; fiscal 1997 and fiscal 2000 are each only partly covered and are not in the 505. For comparison, the World Bank projects API over the same dates returns 597 operations by board approval date, made up of 544 IBRD/IDA, 19 GEF Medium Sized Program, 13 Global Environment Project, 9 Recipient Executed Activities, 4 Debt Reduction Facility, 4 Guarantees, 3 Rainforest and 1 Montreal Protocol, of which 25 rows are supplements or additional financings counted separately - so the API figure is not a lending total and is not comparable with the annual reports' 505.

lawrence-summers.figure_for_owner: World Bank fiscal 1991 and fiscal 1992 (1 July 1990 to 30 June 1992): the Bank's executive directors approved 229 IBRD/IDA lending operations in fiscal 1991 (126 IBRD loans, 103 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1991, Table 7-1) and 222 in fiscal 1992 (112 IBRD loans, 110 IDA credits, World Bank Annual Report 1992, Table 7-1) - 451 over the two years, which is this map's sum of the two reports. What that counts: IBRD loans and IDA credits approved by the Board. Both tables state that supplements are included in the amounts but are not counted as separate lending operations, and that joint IBRD/IDA operations are counted once, as IBRD operations. It excludes IFC and MIGA entirely, and excludes GEF, Montreal Protocol, guarantees, trust-fund activities and debt-reduction operations. Why these two years: the officer lists in the annual reports, dated 30 June 1991 and 30 June 1992, both name 'Lawrence H. Summers, Vice President, Development Economics and Chief Economist', while the list in the 1993 report names 'D.C. Rao (Acting)' in the post, so fiscal 1991 and 1992 are the two full fiscal years in which he is recorded in it; the part of fiscal 1993 he served is not in the 451. For comparison, the World Bank projects API over the same dates returns 309 operations by board approval date, made up of 304 IBRD/IDA, 2 Global Environment Project, 2 Debt Reduction Facility and 1 Montreal Protocol, of which 24 rows are supplements or additional financings counted separately - far below the annual reports' 451 for the same window, so the API's early-1990s coverage appears incomplete and the API figure should not be used here.

lenir-perez.total: As president of Grupo EMCO Holding he headed a group whose assets it put above $700 million for 2021, spanning the Tocoa iron-pellet plant in Honduras and the Palmerola international airport, each a roughly $200 million investment, cargo terminals in El Salvador and Guatemala, cold-chain services and a 100 MW power project (Estrategia y Negocios, December 2021, in a profile commissioned by EMCO Holding, so the figures are the group's own).

sources_add.title: Lenir Perez, presidente del Grupo EMCO Holding: un visionario que lidera importantes proyectos
sources_add.publisher: Revista Estrategia y Negocios (E&N BrandLab, commissioned by EMCO Holding)

lenir-perez.note: Opened the E&N profile. It is explicitly commissioned content ('POR E&N PARA EMCO HOLDING'), so the figures are company-supplied and some are projections; the sentence says so. It gives no count of group companies and no group-wide headcount (only 800 jobs now and 3,000 projected at the Tocoa project). Two better routes failed: EMCO Holding's own site and the Institute of Latin American Studies subsoil-companies entry on Inversiones Los Pinares could not be opened (permission requests unanswered). A UN special-procedures letter of 3 November 2021 about the Guapinol case names only one Los Pinares mining licence and 217 hectares opened to mining inside the Carlos Escaleras national park, which is case detail rather than company scale. A fact-checker should decide whether a sponsored-content asset figure meets the no-fabrication standard; blanking this one would be defensible. ly-yong-phat.total: Rights groups have linked about 40,000 hectares of Cambodian sugar concessions to him: two adjacent Koh Kong concessions granted in 2006 that together formed a 20,000-hectare plantation, whose 2006 concession agreement he signed as chairman of Koh Kong Plantation Co. (Licadho, 2014), and three Oddar Meanchey concessions contracted in January 2008 totalling 19,736 hectares, which the report says are reportedly affiliated with his LYP Group (ActionAid Cambodia and Oxfam, 2015); the roughly 40,000-hectare figure is this map's sum of the two reports.

sources_add.title: Response to Phnom Penh Sugar Company's Allegations Against Equitable Cambodia Executive Director Eang Vuthy (21 August 2014)
sources_add.publisher: Licadho (Cambodian League for the Promotion and Defense of Human Rights)

sources_add.title: The Bitter Taste of Sugar: Displacement and Dispossession in Oddar Meanchey, Cambodia

ly-yong-phat.note: Opened the Licadho statement (dated 21 August 2014) and the ActionAid/Oxfam report (published May 2015, first 100,000 characters). Both are explicit about the limits of the link: Licadho says he divested his Koh Kong sugar shares in December 2009 and is 'clearly affiliated in some way' with the three Oddar Meanchey companies; the ActionAid report rests on reported affiliations (shared head office, villagers told in 2007 to direct complaints about all three companies to him, a commune councillor's 2014 statement). Per-concession hectares in the ActionAid report: Angkor Sugar 6,523, Cambodia Cane and Sugar Valley 6,595, Tonle Sugar Cane 6,618. A Phnom Penh Post article listing six concessions linked to him totalling about 61,000 hectares (including Phnom Penh Sugar 8,343 ha and Kampong Speu Sugar 10,000 ha registered to his wife) was opened but carries no publication date, so it is not cited. The US Treasury designation of 12 September 2024 calls L.Y.P. Group his conglomerate and names four hotels and resorts he owns or controls, but gives no group-scale count. LYP Group's own brochure and profile pages carry no company count, employee count or hectare figure.
